newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - Feb 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - Feb 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Egyptian American Bank is planning to shortly announce the increase of the capital of its mutual fund from 200 million pounds to 300 million.
- A public offer in 30 percent of the capital of a new cement firm, Egypt Cement (Qena), starts today. The 300-million pound issued capital is divided into 30 million shares.
- Alexandria Portland Cement increased pre-tax profits in six months ending on December 31, 1996 to 30 million pounds from 29.5 million in the same period of the previous year.

- Industrial Gases' profits in six months upto December 31, 1996 fell to 2.56 million pounds from 3.45 million in the same period of 1995. 90 percent of the firm was in November offered for sale to one anchor investor through sealed bids. They have not been open yet.

- Telemisr/Arab Radio Transistor and Electronics Supplies made 9.4 million pounds of unaudited net profits in five months, ending on November 30, 1996. No comparison figures were available. The firm's audited net profits in the whole financial year 1995/96 were some 12 million pounds.
- Cairo Housing and Development almost doubled its unaudited pre-tax profits in six months upto December 31, 1996 to 8.31 million pounds from 4.36 million in the same period of the previous year.

- EgyptAir Chairman, Mohamed Fahim Rayan, says the national carrier is not for sale. Rayan denies making a statement, in which he was quoted as saying the firm would either offer 20 percent of its assets for sale or issue new bonds.
